identity.title: Biological Functions of Phytosulfokine Signaling in Plants.

content.abstract: Peptide hormones are signaling molecules that play a crucial role in regulating diverse physiological processes underlying plant growth, development, and stress adaptation. Among these, the widely distributed peptide hormone phytosulfokine (PSK) has emerged as a key regulatory factor. Here, we provide a brief overview of the biosynthesis and characteristics of PSKs. Furthermore, we provide a comprehensive overview of the methodologies for predicting and identifying PSKs in plants and the diverse functions of PSKs in plants. We examine how PSKs govern critical biological processes, including plant growth, root development, and reproduction, and further explore their emerging roles in fruit ripening, senescence, and the mitigation of chilling injury. In addition, the involvement of PSK in both biotic and abiotic stress responses is discussed. Despite significant progress in identifying PSK-related genes through high-throughput approaches, the functional characterization of many remains incomplete. Future research should focus on the application of advanced genetic engineering techniques, such as overexpression, RNA interference, and CRISPR/Cas9, to validate gene functions, elucidate regulatory mechanisms, and identify key transcription factors downstream of PSK signaling. A more comprehensive understanding of these processes will provide a solid foundation for the development of PSK-based strategies in agricultural applications.
